title: Add operator approval proxy, KMS region enforcer and audit coordinator
author: Sofia Bennett
description: Motivation: Provide a guarded pathway for operator-level actions that require explicit approval, guarantee KMS region/pinning constraints are enforced at write-time, and normalize audit artifacts to meet retention and PII-reduction policies. This PR introduces three cooperating components: (1) operator-approval-proxy: an HTTP service and admission hook that requires an approval ticket (canary initially in shadow mode) for privileged API calls; (2) kms-region-enforcer: a lightweight validator (library + admission point) that verifies request context, tenant claims and KMS key metadata to ensure region pinning and policy allowlists are honored; and (3) audit-coordinator: a centralized pipeline stage that canonicalizes audit entries, strips or tokenizes PII per policy, attaches KMS provenance tags, and emits standardized envelopes to the existing audit-forwarder. Design note: RBAC v2 policy templates are extended with two new predicates (operator_action and kms_region_affinity) and a policy-to-admission mapping so the admission controller can make deterministic allow/deny decisions without additional network hops. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy components in shadow mode for 7 days with telemetry and simulated denies (no blocking) to gather metrics and false-positive rate; 2) Run policy-simulator (included) across active traffic; 3) Canary-enforce on a small operator cohort, monitor for elevated denies; 4) Full enforcement by region after 2 successful canaries. Checklist: - [x] Add operator approval proxy service and Helm chart - [x] Implement RBAC v2 predicate extension and policy templates - [x] Add kms-region-enforcer library and admission webhook - [x] Add audit-coordinator pipeline stage and configuration - [x] Provide migration script to convert legacy bindings to new RBAC predicates - [x] Unit tests for policy logic (100% branches) - [x] Integration tests with admission webhooks in CI - [x] Policy linter rules and documentation updates - [x] Telemetry: metrics, traces, and alerts for denial rate, audit-drop_count, and kms_mismatch_count - [ ] Run 7-day shadow rollout and validate with compliance team (post-merge) Backout: revert Helm release and set operator-approval-proxy to shadow mode (one-line rollout toggle). For urgent rollback we also documented a Kubernetes Job (scripts/rollback/disable-approval-proxy.sh) to flip enforcement flags. Security review summary: threat surface limited by mutual TLS to control plane, tokens scoped to operator service account; audit-coordinator runs in a dedicated namespace with read-only access to KMS metadata and no direct decryption privileges (it only attaches provenance tags). Compliance: produces audit envelopes that satisfy retention and pseudonymization guidelines; compliance team provided sign-off for shadow run. Migration notes: includes bin/convert_legacy_bindings.py which maps old role bindings to new predicate-based RBACv2 JSON. Users must run the converter in admin-privileged environment; converter emits dry-run output to help review. Observability: added dashboards in console/observability/operators, and SLO alert playbooks for false-positive spikes. This description intentionally combined design and operational notes to enable reviewers to validate both code and rollout plan.
